feature: Explicit create-only Git reachability pins for saved omdb snapshots

local_compiler.produced_bluefe: not measured in this local qualification

reference_oracle.mode: absolute external executable used only for fixtures and interoperability

local_checks.command: lustr --engine rustc test --manifest-path vendor/sley/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p sley-refs -p sley-gc

differential_slices: SHA-1 and SHA-256, files and reftable
native Rit gc and Git 2.55 gc --prune=now, each first in two hash/ref combinations
unpinned unreachable commit pruned, pinned commit and blob preserved
create-only retries and refusal to overwrite an occupied ref
linked worktree shared common ref namespace
missing descendants and mismatched object link types
on-disk alternates, shared clone, symlinked loose objects, symlinked fanout directories, symlinked packs and promisor pack refusal
review_fixes: reopen object store for post-publication validation; never trust stale caches
reuse Sley fsck typed graph integrity checks alongside strict reachability
reject alternate-owned objects and promisor pack markers
correct documentation of concurrent catalog changes (no omdb CAS for pin)
known_boundaries: no automatic pin release, expiry or catalog-reference reconciliation
no concurrent Git garbage collection or manual object deletion during publication
no cross-store atomicity or independent physical power-loss certification
no multi-tenant security enforcement over an externally mutable Git refs namespace
explicit whole-graph validation can be expensive in large repositories
reused Sley fsck is recursive and may exhaust the process stack for very deep graphs
full Git parity and produced-BlueFe acceptance remain separate work
